Specify newborn group identity inheritance

Source: R/group_inheritance.R
create_group_inheritance.Rd

Assign one group independently of genealogical ancestry shares. Attach this object with fertility() or set_fertility(). The default selects either parent with equal probability, with maternal fallback. Existing people are not reassigned, and ancestry is unchanged by assignment. Fertility also accepts a schedule tibble with time_start, time_end, and a model list column containing complete inheritance objects. Half-open absolute-year intervals select the model at birth; all scheduled possible identities enter one shared registry before execution. See fertility().

Usage

create_group_inheritance(
  method = "random_parent",
  fun = NULL,
  groups = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  passing = 0
)

Arguments

method

One of "mother", "father", "random_parent", "same_sex", "opposite_sex", "ancestry", "hierarchy", or "custom". Random parent chooses each with probability 0.5. Same/opposite sex chooses the parent whose sex matches/differs from the child's. Ancestry samples known child shares, conditioning out unknown ancestry. Missing information required by a built-in rule falls back to the mother, including missing fathers, entirely unknown ancestry, and missing hierarchy ranks.

fun

For "custom", an R function receiving named arguments mother_group, father_group, mother_ancestry, father_ancestry, child_ancestry, child_sex ("f"/"m"), and parents_in_union (logical union status at birth, including on-demand formation). Nonmarital births and unknown fathers give FALSE. Older callbacks without this new argument or ... remain supported. Use ... for unused inputs. Ancestry vectors have group_<label>/unknown names. A missing father has NA group and NULL ancestry. Return exactly one nonmissing identity in the possible group set. Ordinary R random draws are supported; functions must not mutate simulation/global state. Invalid returns and errors fail.

groups

Optional unique group labels extending the inferred possible identities (starting groups plus ancestry groups with positive shares). Declare any additional custom outputs here. Grouped rates and categorical matching levels must cover the complete set before simulation.

order

For "hierarchy", unique group labels, highest-ranked first. Choose between parental identities, not ancestry. Complex orders use fun.

passing

For "hierarchy", probability in [0,1] of reversing the order for a birth. Defaults to zero. Equal parental identities and missing ranks/parents retain maternal assignment without a passing draw.

Value

An inspectable hammel_group_inheritance object.

Examples

create_group_inheritance("mother")
#> $method
#> [1] "mother"
#> 
#> $fun
#> NULL
#> 
#> $groups
#> NULL
#> 
#> $order
#> NULL
#> 
#> $passing
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hammel_group_inheritance"
create_group_inheritance("hierarchy", order = c("A", "B"), passing = 0.05)
#> $method
#> [1] "hierarchy"
#> 
#> $fun
#> NULL
#> 
#> $groups
#> NULL
#> 
#> $order
#> [1] "A" "B"
#> 
#> $passing
#> [1] 0.05
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hammel_group_inheritance"
create_group_inheritance("custom", groups = "mixed",
  fun = function(mother_group, father_group, ...) {
    if (is.na(father_group) || mother_group == father_group) mother_group else "mixed"
  })
#> $method
#> [1] "custom"
#> 
#> $fun
#> function (mother_group, father_group, ...) 
#> {
#>     if (is.na(father_group) || mother_group == father_group) 
#>         mother_group
#>     else "mixed"
#> }
#> <environment: 0xaaabcc727068>
#> 
#> $groups
#> [1] "mixed"
#> 
#> $order
#> NULL
#> 
#> $passing
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "hammel_group_inheritance"
